context_requirements: Expression of Kv channels (e.g., KCNA5, KCNH1/EAG1, KCNQ) or other blocked channels on the cell surface
Membrane potential dependence of proliferation/survival signaling
Intact apoptotic machinery (caspase-3, Apaf-1) for late apoptotic transcriptional output
For KCNH2/hERG-dependent effects, cells must express hERG; most of these lines express it weakly
For RBM3-splicing effects, intracellular potassium perturbation and rG4-containing transcripts must be present
falsifiers: No change in apoptosis-related landmark genes (BAX, PMAIP1, CASP3, GADD45A) at 24 h in any line
No reduction in proliferation/cell-cycle landmark genes (CCNA2, CCNB1, CDK1, AURKA) at 24 h
Strong, uniform transcriptional response across all nine lines including HA1E, which would suggest non-specific toxicity rather than channel-dependent mechanism
Clear response at 6 h that is not sustained or amplified at 24 h, contradicting the slow/apoptotic kinetics
Absence of any stress-response signature (HSPA1A, DNAJB1, ATF5) at 6 h

evidence.supports: Clofilium, a potassium channel blocker, induces caspase-3-dependent apoptosis in HL-60 cells at 10 micromolar, supporting apoptosis as a late transcriptional consequence.
Kv channel blocker 4-aminopyridine induces glioma apoptosis via miR-10b-5p downregulation and Apaf-1/caspase-3 upregulation, supporting pro-apoptotic transcriptional changes.
Voltage-gated potassium channels are overexpressed in breast cancer and regulate proliferation, progression, and apoptosis, supporting context dependence and MCF7 responsiveness.
A potassium channel blocker increases intracellular potassium and alters alternative splicing to raise RBM3, indicating a possible splicing-related transcriptional mechanism.
